title: Merge Two Boarding Lines
statement: Two boarding lines at a gate are linked lists of ticket numbers, each in increasing order. The gate agent joins them into one line in increasing order. Link the existing nodes together, without creating new nodes for the tickets, and return the head of the joined line.
constraints: Both lists are in increasing order (repeats allowed)

answerKey.pattern: Merge by relinking, with a dummy head and a tail pointer
keyPoints: Create a dummy node and a tail pointer at it
While both lists have nodes, attach the smaller front node to tail.next and move that list forward
Move tail to the node just attached
Attach whatever is left of the other list in one step
edgeCases: Equal ticket numbers in both lists
All of one list before the other
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Copy all values to an array, sort, and build a new list: O((n + m) log(n + m)) and O(n + m) space
Recursive merge: O(n + m) time but O(n + m) call stack

hints: The first node of the result is the smaller of the two heads. How do you avoid a special case for it?
Use a dummy node and a tail pointer. Each round, attach the smaller front node to tail.next.
When one list is empty, the other is already sorted: attach it to tail.next and stop.
